reason: Legacy emits server-hostname/server-port when config/dev? is true (the self-hosted image runs in dev mode); dev-only tooling keys.

Legacy serves flushed stream segments as S3 file URLs plus inline content for the buffered tail; this server always inlines content. The reader consumes files-then-content, so delivered bytes are identical (asserted via the folded reader state).

An add-attr step whose attr map is garbage (`{id: "x"}`) reaches the legacy SQL layer and surfaces as a 500 `sql-exception`; this server rejects it as a 400 `validation-failed` on parse. The CLI never sends such a step (its steps come from @instantdb/platform convertTxSteps) and only prints `message` on failure either way.

Legacy silently drops a `delete` step whose eid is a ref lookup (`lookup("primaryOwner.id", <uuid>)`): admin/model.clj expand-delete emits [:delete-entity [attr value] etype], transaction.clj resolve-lookups-for-delete-entity only keeps steps whose lookup resolved through resolve-lookups, and that resolution comes back empty for ref attrs on the live server (verified: the doc stays, tx-id is still returned; plain lookups and the same ref lookup on update/merge/link all resolve). This server resolves ref lookups with the same resolver for every op, so the delete happens. The admin SDK only reads tx-id from the response either way; the divergence is the entity surviving, which is the legacy defect, not a wire shape.

Legacy's deprecated GET /admin/storage/files (db.storage.list) 500s on the self-hosted image (files-get re-dispatches the GET request into query-post with no JSON body, admin/routes.clj:719-737); this server returns the documented StorageFile list (key = S3 object key, name, size, etag/last_modified null). The SDK method is deprecated in favor of querying $files.
